headline: LIMRA projects 2026 U.S. annuity sales to hold above $450 billion after fourth straight record year
summary: LIMRA's latest outlook shows retail annuity sales finishing 2025 above $460 billion, with 2026 sales expected to stay above $450 billion as fixed and fixed-indexed products keep gaining share over traditional variable annuities.

headline: Life insurers enter 2026 with strong capital buffers and steady annuity demand
summary: InvestmentNews reports life insurers begin 2026 on solid footing, citing robust capital strength and continued consumer demand for annuities as key stabilizers for the sector heading into the year.

headline: PayPay completes purchase of majority stake in T&D Financial Life Insurance
summary: Japanese fintech PayPay finalized its acquisition of a 70.2% stake in T&D Financial Life Insurance Company from T&D Holdings, marking a notable fintech entry into life insurance underwriting.

headline: Life and annuity carriers move from AI pilots to permanent transformation in 2026
summary: Industry analysis frames 2026 as the year carriers shift from experimenting with AI in underwriting and fraud prevention toward embedding it permanently, even as regulators push for stronger data integrity and cybersecurity standards.

headline: IRDAI consults industry on insurer-funded policyholder protection fund
summary: India's insurance regulator opened a consultation on whether insurers should make ongoing contributions to a new Policyholders' Education and Protection Fund, with industry comments due mid-July.

headline: Human Interest to take over 401(k) recordkeeping for UBS
summary: Human Interest will provide 401(k) recordkeeping services for UBS, using automated workflows integrated with over 500 payroll providers to track ACH debits, contribution flows, and funding status.

summary: A preview of Vanguard's forthcoming How America Saves 2026 report suggests automatic enrollment and auto-escalation features are pushing account balances to new highs despite market volatility.

summary: The 2026 contribution limit for workers under 50 in job-based retirement accounts rose to $24,500, while workers aged 50-59 and 64-plus gained an $8,000 catch-up allowance, up from $7,500 in 2025.

headline: UK pension risk transfer market on pace for record £70 billion in 2026
summary: Forecasts show the amount of UK defined-benefit pension risk transferred to insurers climbing roughly 15% in 2026 to about £70 billion, with the bulk annuity segment alone expected to top £50 billion for the first time.

headline: US pension risk transfer sales slipped to $49 billion in 2025 even as buy-in deals grew
summary: US pension risk transfer sales fell 6% year-over-year to $49 billion in 2025, but insurers report the buy-in segment kept expanding and expect that trend to continue through 2026.

headline: Insurance asset managers hunt for private-market opportunities as credit spreads stay tight
summary: With traditional credit spreads historically compressed, insurance asset managers are increasingly diversifying into private markets and alternative assets to sustain investment income, per a Pensions & Investments special report.

headline: AXA balances insurance growth against long-term investment ambitions
summary: AXA is weighing continued insurance business expansion against its longer-horizon investment strategy as it navigates a shifting rate and asset-allocation environment.

headline: Mercer flags top investment considerations for insurers navigating 2026
summary: Mercer's 2026 market outlook highlights the investment themes insurers should weigh this year, including rate normalization, private-asset allocation, and portfolio resilience.

headline: Mitigata secures $15 million to expand India cyber insurance underwriting
summary: India-focused insurtech Mitigata raised $15 million to build out cyber insurance coverage and risk-assessment tools for Indian businesses, part of a broader wave of AI-labeled underwriting funding.

headline: RIA M&A hits record $1.67 trillion in deal value in Q1 2026
summary: Echelon Partners reports RIA merger-and-acquisition activity reached a new quarterly record in Q1 2026, with $1.67 trillion in cumulative deal value as consolidation among registered investment advisors accelerates.

headline: Choreo continues acquisition run, adding Illinois-based RIA
summary: Choreo acquired an Illinois registered investment advisor as part of a string of 2026 deals under new CEO Jason Van de Loo, adding roughly $2 billion in combined assets under management this year.

headline: Wealthtech roundup: AI-native platforms and prospecting tools gain traction among large RIAs
summary: A weekly wealthtech roundup covers AI-native wealth manager Arca raising $64 million with backing from Vanguard's former CEO, and a $17 billion RIA naming a money-in-motion prospecting platform as its enterprise-wide tool.

headline: Citi Wealth rolls out AI tools including AskWealth CIO and CitiScribe for advisors
summary: Citi Wealth unveiled new advisor-facing AI capabilities such as Portfolio Intelligence, AskWealth CIO, Client 360 and CitiScribe, aimed at delivering more data-driven, personalized client experiences.

headline: P&C market enters correction phase with significant property rate relief
summary: The U.S. property and casualty market is softening, with a quieter-than-expected 2025 hurricane season and record reinsurance capital driving rate decreases of 10-30% on shared and layered placements versus expiring terms.

headline: Fitch keeps APAC insurance outlook neutral for 2026 despite rising claims costs
summary: Fitch Ratings maintained a neutral 2026 outlook for Asia-Pacific insurers, citing capital buffers and disciplined underwriting offsetting rising claims costs, with non-life premium growth forecast at 2.5%.

headline: Kellen Booher named President & CEO of CopperPoint Insurance
summary: CopperPoint Insurance named Kellen Booher as its new President and CEO, a leadership transition for the workers' compensation-focused P&C carrier.

headline: Progressive CFO to step down in July 2026 after a decade in the role
summary: Progressive's long-serving CFO is set to step down in July 2026, capping roughly 35 years with the auto and property insurer including a decade as chief financial officer.

headline: India raises insurer penalties tenfold under new insurance law amendments
summary: The maximum penalty for violations of India's Insurance Act and IRDAI Act increased tenfold, from ₹1 crore to ₹10 crore, under the newly enacted Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha (Amendment of Insurance Laws) Act.

headline: Acrisure completes acquisition of technology-driven property MGA Vave from Canopius
summary: Acrisure finalized its purchase of Vave, Canopius Group's technology-driven property managing general agent, expanding Acrisure's specialty MGA distribution footprint.

headline: Brown & Brown completes acquisition of specialty MGU Accession Risk Management
summary: Broker Brown & Brown closed its acquisition of Accession Risk Management, a specialty managing general underwriter, broadening its wholesale distribution and underwriting capabilities.

headline: MGA and MGU deal multiples hold firm as sector tops $102 billion in U.S. premium
summary: Lower mid-market MGA and MGU businesses are transacting at 10-14x adjusted EBITDA while platform-scale groups clear 15-22x, as industry estimates put MGAs at more than $102 billion in annual U.S. premium volume.

headline: Specialty group CFC names new group CEO
summary: Specialty insurance group CFC named a new group chief executive expected to join during summer 2026 pending regulatory approval, with a 23-year company veteran serving as acting CEO in the interim.

summary: Corgi Insurance launched Corgi Claims, a full-service TPA pairing a nationwide network of more than 5,000 licensed adjusters with AI that reviews every claim on report, scoring severity and flagging coverage issues and missing documents.

headline: Global insurance TPA market revenue grows by $32 billion year-over-year
summary: A new market report finds the insurance third-party administrator sector's global revenue expanded by roughly $32 billion year-over-year, with AI-driven claims automation cited as a key growth driver through 2030.

headline: Palantir expands AI partnership with Mexico's largest insurer GNP Seguros
summary: Palantir Technologies expanded its enterprise agreement with GNP Seguros, its first publicly announced commercial customer in Latin America, to scale Foundry and AI Platform use across health, life, motor and property lines for fraud detection and claims.

headline: ANNA Money embeds Admiral Business insurance directly into its small-business app
summary: Business account and tax platform ANNA Money partnered with Admiral Business to let small-business customers browse cover options, get information and obtain insurance quotes without leaving the ANNA app.

headline: SquareTrade launches licensed insurer entity in Brussels to reshape European strategy
summary: Warranty and protection-plan provider SquareTrade launched a newly licensed insurance entity in Brussels, bringing underwriting capabilities in-house as it accelerates growth across Europe.

headline: US fintech investment grows in Q2 2026 on 23% jump in larger deals
summary: US fintech investment increased in the second quarter of 2026, driven by a 23% quarter-over-quarter rise in larger funding rounds, signaling renewed investor appetite for scaled fintech platforms.

headline: BrokerTech Ventures names 2026 accelerator cohort of nine insurtech startups
summary: BrokerTech Ventures selected nine insurtech startups for its 2026 accelerator cohort, each receiving $50,000 in seed funding and access to BTV's broker and carrier distribution network to pilot their technology.

headline: BrokerTech Ventures sets September dates for second annual BrokerTech Connect conference
summary: BrokerTech Ventures announced its second annual BrokerTech Connect conference will convene C-suite executives from brokerages, carriers, wholesalers, and insurtech startups in Chicago on September 1-2, 2026.

headline: AI-labeled startups capture record 95.2% of insurtech funding, Gallagher Re finds
summary: Global insurtech investment reached $1.63 billion in Q1 2026, up roughly 27% year-over-year, with AI-labeled companies accounting for a record 95.2% share of total funding according to Gallagher Re.

headline: Poetic raises $50 million Series A for underwriting and compliance automation
summary: Insurtech Poetic secured a $50 million Series A round for its underwriting and compliance automation platform, with investors including Kleiner Perkins, Founders Fund, First Harmonic and OpenAI.

headline: Honeycomb Insurance raises $40 million for digital P&C carrier build-out
summary: Digital P&C insurer Honeycomb Insurance raised $40 million from Zeev Ventures, Ibex Investors, Peakline and other investors to expand its underwriting technology and product lines.

summary: Industry data cited alongside recent insurtech funding rounds shows AI enabling submission-to-quote timelines to shrink from three days to three minutes and straight-through processing rates to jump from 10-15% to 70-90%.

headline: Medicare Advantage penetration holds at 55% as UnitedHealth and Humana near half of enrollment
summary: KFF finds Medicare Advantage penetration steady at 55% as of July 1, 2026, with UnitedHealth Group and Humana together accounting for 46% of enrollees even as UnitedHealth's share slipped and Humana's grew.

summary: Insurers filed proposed 2027 ACA marketplace premiums by the July 15 deadline, with most payers requesting increases in the 10-20% range, setting up another round of affordability debate ahead of open enrollment.

summary: Cigna's Express Scripts settled FTC allegations that it inflated insulin costs through secretive manufacturer deals, agreeing to eliminate spread pricing and delink compensation from drug list prices ahead of 2027 reforms.

summary: New federal legislation delinks pharmacy benefit manager compensation from drug prices in Medicare Part D, shifting to flat 'bona fide service fees' and prohibiting Medicaid spread pricing under a pass-through model.

headline: AI in APAC healthcare enters a new phase in 2026
summary: Asia-Pacific health systems are moving beyond pilot-stage AI deployments in 2026, with broader adoption of clinical decision support and imaging tools across the region's hospitals, per Healthcare IT News.

headline: 27% of health systems now hold commercial AI licenses to ease clinical workload
summary: A new survey finds 27% of U.S. health systems have signed commercial AI licenses aimed at reducing clinician workload, part of a broader push to integrate predictive AI tools with electronic health records.

summary: A July 2026 health IT product roundup highlights new AI radiology draft-reporting tools designed to integrate with existing systems without platform migrations, alongside expanded ambient documentation tools for inpatient nursing workflows.

headline: AI-native insurer Corgi launches full-service claims TPA with 5,000 adjusters
summary: Corgi Insurance rolled out Corgi Claims, a third-party administrator that pairs a nationwide adjuster network with AI that scores severity and flags coverage gaps the instant a claim is filed, serving carriers, MGAs and self-insured programs across major commercial lines.

headline: ANV strikes deal for pan-European travel-protection MGA Assured Underwriting Group
summary: Delegated-underwriting platform ANV agreed to buy London-based Assured Underwriting Group, the UK's top underwriter of travel-insurance bonds, from private-equity owner Mobeus, pending FCA approval expected to close in Q3 2026.

headline: ANV rounds out workers' comp platform with wholesale agency purchase
summary: ANV completed its acquisition of Associated Specialty Insurance Agency, a Pennsylvania wholesale agency with a 600-plus broker network focused on artisan contractor workers' comp risk, deepening ANV's specialty comp distribution alongside two other recent buys.

headline: Allianz eyes Portuguese insurer Caravela in deal that could nearly triple its local market share
summary: Allianz is reportedly in advanced talks to buy Caravela Seguros, Portugal's seventh-largest non-life insurer, a move that would lift Allianz's non-life market share in the country from roughly 1.3% to nearly 7% and push it past €1.15 billion in combined premiums.

headline: AIG formally hands CEO reins to Eric Andersen as Zaffino moves to board chair
summary: AIG completed its planned leadership succession, with Eric Andersen becoming chief executive and joining the board while outgoing CEO Peter Zaffino shifts into the role of executive chairman.

headline: US P&C insurers post strong 92.4 combined ratio as premium growth cools sharply
summary: Verisk and APCIA reported that US property-casualty carriers notched a 92.4 combined ratio and roughly $15.8 billion in underwriting gains for Q1 2026, even as premium growth decelerated markedly from prior years.

summary: Connie Health closed a $40 million Series B led by HealthQuest Capital while simultaneously completing its tenth acquisition, absorbing Clearlink Insurance Agency's Medicare business to scale its AI-driven senior-enrollment platform.

summary: Centene confirmed it is offering a voluntary separation program across the bulk of its employee base as the Medicaid-focused insurer works to cut costs amid declining earnings.

summary: CMS proposed converting the IRA's Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program into binding federal regulation starting plan year 2029 and opened comment on a framework requiring PBMs to report detailed drug pricing and rebate data.

headline: IRDAI orders health insurers and hospitals onto new claims-speed and billing scorecards
summary: India's insurance regulator introduced performance scorecards tracking claim settlement speed and billing accuracy for insurers and hospitals, alongside simpler standardized health policies meant to boost low insurance penetration.

headline: IRDAI chief says Bima Sugam marketplace will offer its first policies by September
summary: IRDAI chairman Ajay Seth said the long-awaited Bima Sugam digital insurance marketplace will launch initial motor, health and term products by end-September, with a separate consultation on distribution reforms due by end-July.

headline: IRDAI proposes letting insurers park up to 5% of surplus capital in private companies
summary: India's regulator floated rules allowing insurers to invest a portion of shareholder funds beyond the solvency margin into private limited companies, plus new repo and securities-lending powers for life insurers to manage liquidity.

headline: Allianz Retire+ hires senior distribution lead as its guaranteed-income annuity gains adviser traction
summary: Allianz Retire+ reported a 31% jump in uptake of its AGILE lifetime-income product since January and named a new senior manager for retirement solutions to build on the momentum following recent fee cuts and product enhancements.

headline: Modern Wealth notches 22nd deal with $1.1B Florida RIA acquisition
summary: Modern Wealth Management agreed to acquire Clearwater-based Flaharty Asset Management, adding roughly $1.1 billion in client assets and an 18-person team as it pushes total AUM past $14 billion.

headline: Waverly Advisors makes first trust-company purchase, buying $3B Smithfield Trust
summary: Birmingham-based Waverly Advisors acquired Pittsburgh's Smithfield Trust Company in its first dedicated trust acquisition, pushing the RIA's total assets under management well past $35 billion.

headline: Modera Wealth adds $312M Florida RIA to expand state footprint
summary: Modera Wealth Management, a roughly $17.5 billion RIA, agreed to acquire Northstar Financial Planners, a Florida-based advisory firm managing about $311.6 million in client assets.

headline: Creative Planning deepens Southwest Florida push with accounting-firm acquisition
summary: National RIA Creative Planning agreed to acquire MarkhamNorton Accountants+Advisors, a 45-year-old Southwest Florida tax and advisory firm, in a deal expected to close July 1.

summary: NatWest completed its acquisition of Evelyn Partners, combining Evelyn's £69 billion in assets under management with NatWest's £59 billion private banking book to form a roughly £127 billion combined wealth platform.

summary: At the 8th Annual RPA Record Keeper Roundtable, industry leaders described a squeeze between shrinking fees and rising demands for AI, cybersecurity and expanded participant services, while eyeing financial wellness as a growth avenue.

summary: BlackRock said it will liquidate its LifePath ESG Index Retirement Fund in October, leaving only Fidelity and GuideStone as managers still offering a dedicated sustainable target-date fund.

headline: Submissions-tool startup Sytrex rebrands as Braven after $4.6M seed and London launch
summary: Formerly known as Sytrex, the insurance infrastructure startup raised a $4.6 million seed round led by Collide Capital, rebranded as Braven, and opened a London office to chase delegated-authority and specialty business.

headline: Nassau Financial backs AI-governance startup Trussed AI through its Reimagine program
summary: Nassau Financial Group made an undisclosed investment in Trussed AI, a platform that helps regulated enterprises audit and govern their AI systems, via Nassau's insurtech-focused Reimagine venture program.

headline: IAG's venture arm backs crisis-support app Sonder to extend care beyond claims
summary: Australia's IAG made a strategic minority investment in Sonder through its Firemark Ventures arm, aiming to extend the 24/7 mental-health and safety platform to customers during catastrophic weather events, not just its own workforce.

headline: Goldman Sachs leads $110M round for AI decisioning startup Taktile eyeing insurance claims
summary: Taktile raised a $110 million Series C led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives with Tiger Global and Index Ventures participating, positioning its AI decisioning platform to speed up high-stakes banking and insurance-claims calls.

headline: HSBC signs multi-year AI alliance with Google Cloud
summary: HSBC entered a multi-year partnership with Google Cloud to embed AI more deeply across its banking and financial-services operations as part of a broader industry push toward cloud-based AI infrastructure.

headline: Ascension closes $3.9B AmSurg surgery-center deal after FTC-ordered divestitures
summary: Ascension completed its acquisition of ambulatory surgery operator AmSurg after agreeing to divest seven surgery centers to resolve FTC antitrust concerns, growing its ASC network to 300 centers across 35 states.

summary: HCA Healthcare acquired 17 urgent care clinics from Urgent Care Group across Charleston, Columbia, Myrtle Beach and Wilmington, rebranding them under its CareNow banner and pushing its urgent-care network past 390 locations.

headline: WellSpan Health signs seven-year imaging and AI partnership with Philips
summary: WellSpan Health launched a seven-year alliance with Philips to advance diagnostic imaging, AI-enabled tools and broader clinical innovation across its health system.

headline: Private Equity Firm Flexpoint Ford Takes Stake in Insurance Carrier Platform Novel Financial
summary: Flexpoint Ford invested in Novel Financial Holdings, an independent holding company backing managing general underwriters and carriers that write roughly $2 billion in annual premium, broadening Novel's ownership base as it scales.

summary: With India's insurance FDI limit raised to 100%, IRDAI has already cleared one foreign investor's bid to raise its stake in a domestic venture and is reviewing another, signaling accelerating foreign entry into the market.

summary: Target-date fund series that embed guaranteed-income annuities grew nearly 70% year-over-year to about $42 billion across 13 series by the end of March 2026, with BlackRock's LifePath Paycheck line driving much of the gain.

headline: Wisconsin Retirement System Resets Retiree Insurance Premium Deduction Timing
summary: Wisconsin's Department of Employee Trust Funds implemented a one-time reset of annuity-deducted health and life insurance premiums for WRS retirees in July 2026 ahead of full payment-schedule alignment in August.

summary: Coastal Bridge Advisors completed a three-way combination with Waddell & Associates and One Charles Private Wealth, creating a single advisory firm with more than $10 billion in assets across seven offices.

summary: Orion Advisor Solutions earned ISO/IEC 42001 certification for the AI management system behind its Denali intelligence layer, joining a small group of tech firms with the credential.

summary: The two wealthtech vendors are combining AI-driven workflow automation with aggregated, compliant portfolio data to help wealth managers streamline front-to-back-office operations and cut costs.

summary: Brokers reported risk-adjusted price cuts of roughly 15-40% across U.S. property treaty and facultative placements at the July 1 renewal date, as abundant capital and strong reinsurer profits softened the market.

headline: Global Reinsurance Capital Hits Record $790 Billion, Tilting Leverage to Buyers
summary: A surge in traditional and alternative capital pushed global reinsurer capital to an all-time high heading into the mid-year renewals, strengthening cedents' negotiating position on price and terms.

headline: California's Insurance Chief Wins Court Fight Over Market-Stabilization Bulletins
summary: A Los Angeles judge rejected a Consumer Watchdog lawsuit challenging Commissioner Ricardo Lara's bulletins limiting how much FAIR Plan wildfire losses insurers can pass on to policyholders, upholding his stabilization approach.

summary: New industry research shows shifts in coverage language and provisions are suppressing the number of claims filed, an underappreciated factor reshaping loss-cost trends across personal and commercial lines.

summary: ANV Group completed its acquisition of Iris Insurance Brokers, combining a Lloyd's wholesale brokerage, an intermediary platform and an MGA incubator to expand its UK and European specialty distribution reach.

summary: The Managing General Agents' Association appointed Tim Smyth to succeed Charles Manchester as chairman following ten years in the role, effective around the trade body's annual conference.

summary: Amwins Specialty Casualty Solutions acquired Jackson-Lloyd, a pioneer in non-subscriber occupational accident programs for Texas employers, adding to its accident and health portfolio.

summary: Arthur J. Gallagher acquired Burnaby-based commercial broker Wilson M. Beck Insurance Services in a deal described as among the largest ever completed in the Canadian market, deepening its construction and surety practices.

headline: IRDAI Plans to Overhaul Agent Commission Structure to Curb Mis-Selling
summary: India's insurance regulator is preparing a consultation paper that would spread distributor commissions over a policy's full life instead of paying them upfront, aiming to reduce mis-selling driven by front-loaded incentives.

headline: Goldman-Led $110 Million Round Backs AI-Native Claims Automation Startup
summary: A major funding round led by Goldman Sachs backed an AI claims automation platform that one large insurer is reportedly piloting to save more than $90 million, underscoring AI's dominance of insurtech investment dollars.

headline: Startup Corgi Launches AI-Native Platform to Speed Up Insurance Claims
summary: Insurtech Corgi unveiled a new AI-driven platform designed to accelerate claims handling end-to-end for insurers.

summary: Horizon Blue Cross Blue Shield of New Jersey began accepting proposals on July 1, 2026 for its HealthEZ third-party administration platform targeting mid-sized self-funded employers, with plans taking effect January 1, 2027.

summary: CMS's new Medicare GLP-1 Bridge took effect July 1, 2026, giving eligible Part D beneficiaries with qualifying conditions access to drugs like Zepbound and Wegovy for a flat $50 monthly copay through the end of 2027.

summary: A growing number of hospitals and health systems are dropping certain Medicare Advantage contracts in 2026, citing persistent prior-authorization denials and slow reimbursement from payers.

summary: HOPPR commercially launched Presto, an AI reporting agent that drafts radiology reports directly inside existing systems like PowerScribe without requiring new software or platform migrations.

summary: Ambience Healthcare introduced Nursing Summary and Ambient Flowsheet Documentation tools that convert a nurse's spoken patient assessment directly into structured EHR entries, extending its inpatient AI system from pre-shift prep through charting.

summary: Independence Health System's Butler Memorial Hospital is on track to join WVU Medicine this fall under a merger agreement that includes an $800 million capital investment, with $165 million earmarked specifically for Butler's facilities.

headline: Fixed annuity rates hold near 15-year highs even as Fed easing looms
summary: Top multi-year guaranteed annuity rates are sitting around 6.3%, well above comparable CD yields, though brokers expect rates to soften gradually as the Federal Reserve continues cutting.

headline: Empower to absorb Milliman's retirement recordkeeping arm in $340 million deal
summary: Empower agreed to buy Milliman's retirement and benefits administration business, picking up roughly 1,100 defined-contribution plans and 400 defined-benefit plans covering more than $130 billion in combined assets, while Milliman keeps its actuarial consulting unit.

summary: Assets in target-date strategies embedding annuities nearly doubled year over year to about $44 billion, yet that remains under 1% of the broader $4.8 trillion target-date market as plan sponsors continue weighing guaranteed-income options.

summary: Second-quarter inflows into US-listed ETFs hit a record $560 billion, pushing first-half totals over $1 trillion and putting the industry on pace for roughly $2.3 trillion for the full year, per State Street's flow data.

headline: Savant Wealth Management plants its flag in Maine via Richard Brothers tie-up
summary: Savant closed a partnership with South Portland-based Richard Brothers Financial Advisors, adding about $240 million in client assets and giving the RIA its first Maine office among 70 locations nationwide.

headline: Singapore regulator floats protected-cell structure to grow alternative risk transfer
summary: MAS opened a consultation on a protected cell company framework meant to let Singapore compete for captive insurance, insurance-linked securities and sovereign risk-pooling business, running through early August.

headline: Goldman Sachs leads $110M round for AI decisioning startup serving banks and insurers

summary: Mitigata, an IRDAI-regulated cyber insurance broker serving over 800 organizations, raised a $15 million Series B led by Bessemer Venture Partners to expand its combined security, compliance and insurance platform.

headline: France's KAPIA-RGI snaps up Cegid Assurex to widen personal insurance software suite
summary: KAPIA-RGI acquired Cegid Assurex Solutions, adding capabilities across annuities, provident benefits, retirement savings and tax-withholding administration to its personal insurance software offering in France.

summary: Northwell Health completed its merger with Nuvance Health, forming a combined system of 28 hospitals and over 1,000 care sites with $22.6 billion in revenue and more than 100,000 employees.

summary: Ambience Healthcare rolled out a Nursing Suite adding automated shift summaries and ambient flowsheet documentation, aiming to cut manual charting burden for inpatient nurses while keeping clinicians reviewing every entry.

headline: UK regulator's funded reinsurance crackdown could reshape bulk annuity deals
summary: The Bank of England's Prudential Regulation Authority is pushing ahead with Consultation Paper CP8/26, which would roughly double or more the capital insurers must hold against funded reinsurance used heavily in pension risk transfer deals; the consultation window closes July 31, 2026.

headline: Fidelity to bolt guaranteed lifetime income onto its target-date fund lineup
summary: Fidelity is launching Freedom Lifetime, a suite of target-date collective investment trusts that let plan sponsors offer employees the option to convert part of their target-date balance into a guaranteed income stream, available on Fidelity's recordkeeping platform in early 2027.

headline: Hightower's acquisitive Signature Wealth unit lands three more advisory teams worth $5 billion
summary: Hightower's Signature Wealth division added Private Vista, Hightower Great Lakes and The McGuirk & De Nevi Group in a combined deal bringing roughly $5 billion in assets, pushing its year-to-date total past $25 billion added through conversions and acquisitions.

headline: Wealth Enhancement adds an 88-year-old New York advisory shop in a $760 million deal
summary: National RIA aggregator Wealth Enhancement agreed to acquire the Shufro-Glass Group from Shufro Rose, a firm founded in 1938, adding more than $760 million in client assets and pushing Wealth Enhancement's total assets above $157 billion.

headline: New York rolls out fresh guidance aimed at bringing down auto insurance premiums
summary: Governor Hochul directed the state's Department of Financial Services to issue new guidance implementing FY2027 budget reforms intended to lower New York auto insurance rates and crack down on fraudulent claims, effective July 1.

headline: Allegheny Health Network's insurance parent finances hospital tie-up with $285 million pledge
summary: As Heritage Valley Health System formally joined Allegheny Health Network on July 1, insurer parent Highmark and the merging systems jointly committed roughly $285 million over a decade to fund clinical and IT upgrades, underscoring how payer-provider capital is intertwined in the deal.

headline: Catastrophe-property MGU pulls in $460 million-plus as admitted carriers retreat from Florida and Texas
summary: A continuation vehicle led by Lexington Partners and Barings poured more than $460 million into a catastrophe-exposed property managing general underwriter, capital meant to let it keep writing coverage in states where standard insurers are pulling back.

headline: Lloyd's MGA launches data-backed deductible buy-down cover for renewable energy sites
summary: Africa Speciality Risks, a Lloyd's MGA, launched what it calls the world's first data-enabled deductible buy-down product for renewable energy assets, giving brokers independently verified real-time asset data to negotiate better underwriting terms.

headline: Acrisure's UK arm loses its CEO and CFO/COO in abrupt leadership shake-up
summary: Acrisure UK chief executive Mark Mcilquham and CFO/COO Katherine Cross both had their roles terminated, with interim leadership handed to Andrew Boyce and Eleanor Gamble as the broker platform's UK retail business regroups.

headline: DOL's proposed PBM fee-disclosure rule set to reach TPAs for plan years starting July 2026
summary: A Department of Labor proposal would force pharmacy benefit managers and the TPAs and insurers that administer PBM services for self-funded ERISA health plans to make detailed compensation disclosures, with applicability proposed for plan years beginning on or after July 1, 2026.
source_name: U.S. Department of Labor / Federal Register

headline: Matic scoops up Policygenius' home and auto book alongside new PE backing
summary: Embedded insurance platform Matic secured a minority growth investment from Primus Capital while simultaneously acquiring nearly 30,000 property and casualty policies from Policygenius, folding those customers into its 70-plus carrier marketplace.

headline: Vertafore rolls out AI agents to automate agency email and reconciliation work
summary: Vertafore released two new Velocity AI agents built into its AgencyOne platform, one handling inbound email triage and one automating reconciliation, with early testing showing up to 80% faster email processing for independent agencies.

headline: Bengaluru cyber-insurance startup Mitigata raises $15 million Series B led by Bessemer
summary: Mitigata, which combines cybersecurity monitoring with cyber insurance for Indian businesses, closed a $15 million Series B led by Bessemer Venture Partners to expand internationally and scale its AI-powered security operations center.

headline: New York's Essential Plan cliff hits roughly 450,000 immigrant enrollees this month
summary: About 450,000 New Yorkers, largely lawfully present immigrants, lost Essential Plan coverage as of July 1 after federal budget law changes eliminated their ACA subsidy eligibility, pushing them onto marketplace plans with premiums and cost-sharing.

headline: Value-based Medicare tech firm Pearl Health raises $110 million to expand payer partnerships
summary: Pearl Health closed a $110 million raise, a $50 million equity round led by Andreessen Horowitz plus a $60 million credit facility, to grow its AI clinical intelligence platform used by providers and payers managing Medicare risk contracts.

headline: US age-adjusted death rate hits a record low as CDC releases fresh 2025 data
summary: Provisional CDC data published July 2 showed the nation's age-adjusted death rate fell 4.6% in 2025 to 689.2 per 100,000 people, the lowest rate ever recorded, a data point providers and payers are citing in mortality and underwriting trend discussions.
source_name: Alston & Bird (Health Care Week in Review)

headline: ICICI Prudential Life seeks reclassification of Prudential as investor amid Bharti Life buyout
summary: As Prudential moves to take a 75% controlling stake in Bharti Life Insurance, ICICI Prudential Life's board asked regulators to reclassify Prudential Corporation Holdings from a promoter to an investor and is weighing a rename to ICICI Life, with both promoters signing a letter of undertaking on July 4 to manage the conflict of interest.

headline: Allianz and Zurich launch joint blended-finance vehicle with government backers
summary: Allianz and Zurich, alongside AXA and Canadian pension giant La Caisse, launched Scaled Development, a platform meant to mobilize private capital for sustainable projects in emerging markets, with Germany and Canada committing initial public capital of up to €130 million.

headline: European wealth managers rethink how they welcome crypto-derived fortunes
summary: Private banks including Dutch wealth manager Van Lanschot Kempen are shifting from treating crypto wealth holders with suspicion to actively courting them, pairing compliance specialists with family-office style services to capture the 'new wealthy.'

headline: WealthTech leads another active week of fintech fundraising
summary: Wealthtech startups accounted for five of the 17 fintech funding deals tracked in the first days of July, continuing a strong run for advisor- and RIA-focused technology investment following a record Q1 for the category.

headline: Swiss Re projects sharpest slowdown in global non-life premium growth in over a decade
summary: Swiss Re Institute forecasts real non-life premium growth will slow to just 0.6% in 2026, far below the 3.6% long-term trend, as competitive pricing and softer economic momentum weigh on advanced markets while insurer ROE eases from its 2025 peak.

headline: JPMorgan sees no floor yet for falling reinsurance prices after steep midyear drop
summary: JPMorgan analysts say property catastrophe reinsurance rates fell roughly 16% at the July 1 renewal, an acceleration from January, as record capital and low catastrophe losses continue shifting pricing power toward cedents with little sign of stabilizing.

headline: Willis Re adds veteran marine broker to reinsurance team
summary: Willis Re hired David Kim, a 20-year marine and non-marine reinsurance veteran and former Korean Re London chief executive, as a reinsurance broker to bolster its marine practice.

headline: MGAA installs Bspoke Group's Tim Smyth as new chairman
summary: The UK's Managing General Agents' Association named Tim Smyth, chair of Bspoke Group, as its new chairman, succeeding Charles Manchester after his decade-long tenure leading the trade body.

headline: Alliant lures former Hub executive to lead expanded M&A advisory push
summary: Alliant Insurance Services named Justin Sorensen, formerly a Hub International practice leader, to the newly created role of executive vice president within Alliant's mergers and acquisitions advisory team, reporting to the president of Alliant P&C.

headline: White Glove Insurance spins up brokerage tech subsidiary
summary: White Glove Insurance launched White Glove Technology, a new subsidiary building a full-service platform meant to consolidate the fragmented vendor stack independent brokerages rely on, with a phased rollout planned through Q4 2026.

headline: Goldman-led $110 million round backs AI claims automation platform Taktile
summary: Goldman Sachs led a $110 million investment into Taktile, with one major insurer reportedly modeling more than $90 million in claims savings from adopting the AI decisioning platform, in one of the quarter's largest insurtech rounds.

headline: Insurers' AI pilots keep stalling before they reach production
summary: A growing share of insurer AI pilots fail to graduate into production deployments, with industry analysts pointing to weak data foundations and unclear ROI cases as the main reasons projects stall despite heavy AI investment across the sector.

headline: New Indian institute launches insurtech leadership training program at GIFT City
summary: NeoProEd kicked off the first cohort of its Insurtech Professional Program in partnership with GIFT International FinTech Institute, a 10-week practitioner-led course capped by a residential capstone in Gandhinagar aimed at building India's next generation of insurance and insurtech leaders.

headline: Asia's largest insurtech gathering spotlights agentic AI and underinsurance
summary: ITC Asia 2026 drew more than 1,500 industry leaders to Singapore for sessions on turning agentic AI into measurable underwriting and claims ROI, alongside dedicated tracks on Japan's evolving insurance ecosystem and expanding coverage across India.

headline: Medicare beneficiaries get $50-a-month GLP-1 weight-loss drug access under new CMS bridge program
summary: CMS's new Medicare GLP-1 Bridge program, which took effect July 1, lets eligible Part D beneficiaries access Wegovy and Zepbound for weight management at a flat $50 monthly copay through the end of 2027, marking the first time Medicare has covered GLP-1s for weight loss.

headline: Florida's top cancer center drops out of Humana Medicare Advantage network
summary: Moffitt Cancer Center became out-of-network for Humana Medicare Advantage PPO and HMO plans starting July 1, forcing Tampa-area cancer patients to weigh higher out-of-pocket costs or switch coverage, though Humana may extend continuity-of-care exceptions through year-end.

headline: Judge forces Mississippi Medicaid to pay Delta hospital to avert closure
summary: A Mississippi Chancery Court judge ordered the state's Medicaid division to release a $2.4 million payment to Greenwood Leflore Hospital, averting an imminent shutdown while a planned takeover by the University of Mississippi Medical Center proceeds.

headline: OpenAI leans on Sam Altman to court hospitals for its healthcare push
summary: OpenAI is pitching hospitals directly, with CEO Sam Altman personally engaging health systems, as the company rolls out ChatGPT for Clinicians and a consumer 'ChatGPT Health' feature while competing with Anthropic and Google for enterprise healthcare business.

headline: High earners lean on HSAs over 401(k) catch-ups as new Roth mandate takes effect
summary: With 2026's requirement that catch-up contributions from workers earning over $150,000 be made on a Roth basis, advisors report high earners are increasingly prioritizing HSA contributions first for their triple tax advantage.

headline: Lemonade trims reinsurance cession again in latest July renewal
summary: Lemonade reduced its quota-share cession to roughly 18% of premium from about 20% in its July 1, 2026 reinsurance renewal, a smaller adjustment than last year's steep cut, while expanding its European catastrophe protection.

headline: MGA premiums surge to $108.7 billion in 2025 as capacity providers grow choosier
summary: AM Best's annual MGA segment report found delegated-authority premium jumped nearly 18% in 2025, marking a fifth straight year of double-digit growth, though analysts flagged tighter carrier scrutiny of capacity deployment ahead.

headline: AI-linked layoffs ripple through tech and finance sectors, insurance included
summary: A labor-market analysis found tech and finance employers, including insurance-adjacent firms, are shedding roughly 28,000 jobs a month as AI automation reshapes staffing needs across broker and carrier back offices.

headline: Allianz Partners to cut up to 1,800 jobs as it leans further into AI
summary: Allianz's travel-and-assistance unit confirmed plans to eliminate as many as 1,800 European roles as part of a broader push to adopt AI across claims and customer service operations.

headline: ACA marketplace insurers propose another double-digit premium jump for 2027
summary: A KFF analysis of 77 insurers' rate filings found a median proposed 2027 ACA premium increase of 14%, following 2026's 20% median hike, driven by rising costs, regulatory changes and the expiration of enhanced subsidies.

headline: Roughly 450,000 immigrants lose New York's Essential Plan coverage as eligibility rules tighten
summary: New York's Essential Plan enrollees between 200-250% of the federal poverty level, including many lawfully present immigrants, lost coverage on July 1, 2026 after federal changes eliminated the subsidies that made the expanded program financially viable.

headline: MemorialCare's longtime CEO Barry Arbuckle steps up to executive chairman
summary: After more than two decades leading MemorialCare, Barry Arbuckle moved into a new executive chairman role effective July 1, 2026, with Dr. David Kim succeeding him as president and CEO in a long-planned succession.

headline: UK unveils new framework to cut heart disease and stroke deaths
summary: The UK government launched a Cardiovascular Disease Modern Service Framework setting 12 near-term priorities aimed at preventing thousands of premature heart disease and stroke deaths annually through earlier diagnosis and more consistent care.

headline: AI tool wins first-of-its-kind FDA clearance for detecting hidden heart disease from routine ECGs
summary: Pathway Labs' EchoNext became the first FDA-cleared AI tool to flag six types of structural heart disease from a standard 12-lead ECG, trained on hundreds of thousands of paired ECG-echocardiogram records and now being distributed via OpenEvidence.

headline: MassMutual climbs to No. 100 on Fortune 500 in its 175th anniversary year
summary: MassMutual announced it rose to No. 100 on the 2026 Fortune 500 list, extending a streak of more than three decades on the ranking as the mutual insurer marks 175 years in business.

headline: Wealth Enhancement scoops up second Shufro Rose team with $554 million in assets
summary: Wealth Enhancement agreed to acquire the Kaminsky-Silverman Group from New York-based Shufro Rose, its second deal with the firm in as many months, adding roughly $554 million in client assets.

headline: Softening P&C market fuels fresh megadeal speculation, with Zurich-Beazley as bellwether
summary: Dealmakers point to Zurich's $10.9 billion all-cash agreement to acquire Lloyd's insurer Beazley as a sign more billion-dollar-plus insurance acquisitions could surface in the second half of 2026 as underwriting conditions soften.

headline: Property catastrophe reinsurance rates fall as much as 20% at mid-year Florida renewals
summary: Record capital from traditional and alternative sources pushed risk-adjusted property-catastrophe reinsurance pricing down roughly 15-20% at the June/July renewals, even as Florida cedents sought billions more in coverage.

headline: Singapore regulator floats protected cell company framework for alternative risk transfer
summary: The Monetary Authority of Singapore opened a consultation on a new Protected Cell Company legislative structure meant to deepen alternative risk transfer and collateralized reinsurance activity in the city-state.

headline: Acrisure folds six specialty MGAs into new Asero Insurance Services brand
summary: Acrisure launched Asero Insurance Services to unify several of its program administrators, which collectively underwrite over $1 billion in premium for hard-to-place commercial risks, under one shared platform.

headline: CFC recruits former Direct Line chief Adam Winslow as group CEO
summary: Specialty MGA CFC named Adam Winslow, formerly group CEO of Direct Line Group, as its next chief executive, succeeding Louise O'Shea as the company looks to accelerate international growth and AI adoption.

headline: Virginia's tougher PBM and TPA oversight law takes effect
summary: A new Virginia law effective July 1, 2026 expands regulation of PBMs and third-party administrators, banning practices like retroactive claim reductions and electronic claim-processing fees while mandating pass-through pricing.

headline: Bengaluru cyber insurance startup Mitigata lands $15 million Series B
summary: Mitigata, an IRDAI-regulated cyber insurance broker, raised a $15 million Series B led by Bessemer Venture Partners to expand its AI-powered cyber resilience platform internationally and scale its security operations center.

headline: Matic buys Policygenius's 30,000-policy home and auto book, adds Primus Capital as investor
summary: Embedded insurance platform Matic acquired Policygenius's property and casualty insurance portfolio of nearly 30,000 policies and secured a minority growth investment from Primus Capital to fund further expansion.

headline: NeoProEd launches to close India's insurtech talent gap
summary: NeoProEd, founded by veteran insurance leaders, launched its Insurtech Professional Program with the GIFT International FinTech Institute to train talent for India's fast-growing, AI- and embedded-insurance-driven sector.

headline: Brian Evanko takes the reins as Cigna's new CEO
summary: Brian Evanko officially became CEO of The Cigna Group on July 1, succeeding David Cordani, who moves into the role of executive chair after nearly 17 years leading the company.

headline: ACA marketplace enrollment drops by millions as subsidy fight continues
summary: With enhanced ACA premium subsidies expired, marketplace enrollment has fallen by millions, and the Trump administration and policy analysts continue to disagree over how much of the drop reflects affordability versus fraud crackdowns.

headline: Elevance sues CMS seeking same Medicare Advantage star-rating fix given to Clover
summary: Elevance Health sued CMS and HHS, arguing it deserves the same star-ratings recalculation a court forced for Clover Health, a change Elevance says would be worth about $115 million in quality bonus payments.

headline: India's insurance regulator floats spreading agent commissions across a policy's full life
summary: IRDAI is considering replacing large upfront commissions with payouts spread over the life of a policy to curb mis-selling, with a distribution consultation paper expected by end of July according to chairman Ajay Seth.

headline: Steward Partners taps Sequoia Financial's Joseph Glick as new COO
summary: Steward Partners, which now oversees more than $53 billion in assets, hired Joseph Glick away from Sequoia Financial Group to run operations, technology and finance as the firm scales.

headline: Hybrid RIA AmeriFlex reaches its $3 billion growth target six months ahead of schedule
summary: The AmeriFlex Group added 18 advisors and more than $1.7 billion in client assets in the first half of 2026, crediting succession-matching tools for pulling forward its annual growth goal.

headline: US P&C insurers swing to $16.3 billion underwriting gain in strongest Q1 in decades
summary: The US property-casualty industry posted a $16.3 billion net underwriting gain in Q1 2026, reversing a year-earlier loss on lower catastrophe losses and easing incurred-loss trends, according to AM Best data.

headline: UK underwriting body warns dealmakers are leaning too hard on cyber cover
summary: The International Underwriting Association cautioned that warranty-and-indemnity insurers may be over-relying on cyber insurance to cover M&A transaction risk, flagging coverage gaps underwriters need to address.

headline: Pen Underwriting doubles UK SME cyber cover to £10 million as broker demand rises
summary: MGA Pen Underwriting raised its cyber cover limit to £10 million for risks incepting from July 1 and brought claims handling in-house, responding to broker demand from larger SME clients.

headline: Specialist Risk Group snaps up London MGA and wholesale broker Superian
summary: SRG acquired Superian Insurance Group, a London wholesaler, retailer and MGA known for medical malpractice and healthcare liability expertise, expanding SRG's specialist distribution capacity.

headline: Liberty Mutual elevates Defne Turkes to lead its international insurance division
summary: Liberty Mutual named Defne Turkes president and managing director of Liberty International Insurance effective July 1, tasking her with growth across commercial and Asia retail markets.

headline: Aon installs Pedro Penalva as new CEO of Latin America
summary: Aon named Pedro Penalva CEO of Latin America effective July 1, reporting directly to CEO Greg Case, as part of a broader regional leadership reshuffle spanning EMEA and Latin America.

headline: MGA platform Novel Financial Holdings lands strategic backing from Flexpoint Ford
summary: Novel Financial Holdings, which oversees carriers writing about $2 billion in annual premium tied to managing general underwriters, received a growth investment from private equity firm Flexpoint Ford.

headline: Point32Health's TPA arm HPI names Tim O'Brien as president
summary: Health Plans, Inc., a national third-party administrator of self-funded benefit plans, appointed Tim O'Brien president, bringing experience from leading Vitori Health through its sale to Global Excel Management.

headline: Independent agency Barge Group consolidates quoting on EZLynx's rating platform
summary: Barge Group adopted EZLynx's integrated personal-lines rater to enter risk data once and pull real-time quotes from multiple carriers, aiming to speed proposals and free up time for prospecting.

headline: Insurance Journal previews industry 'Demo Day' showcasing agentic AI underwriting tools
summary: Insurance Journal spotlighted an upcoming Risky Future event where vendors will demo agentic AI tools built for underwriting, part of a broader industry push to move AI pilots into production for policy pricing.

headline: Claims-communication insurtech Kyber named a 2026 PropertyCasualty360 Insurance Luminary
summary: Kyber was recognized in PropertyCasualty360's 2026 Insurance Luminaries class for workplace culture, with founder and CEO Arvind Sontha honored as Rising Star of the Year.

headline: China issues first nationwide AI rulebook for banks and insurers
summary: China's National Financial Regulatory Administration published guidelines spanning governance, data handling and risk management for AI use across the banking and insurance sectors, its first comprehensive framework of its kind.

headline: Medicare's $50-a-month GLP-1 weight-loss drug bridge takes effect July 1
summary: Medicare Part D beneficiaries meeting BMI and health-condition criteria can now access GLP-1 obesity medications like Wegovy and Zepbound for $50 a month through 2027 under a new CMS pilot tied to manufacturer pricing deals.

headline: Payer stocks extend rally as UnitedHealth and Centene guidance eases cost-trend fears
summary: UnitedHealth shares have climbed roughly 78% off their yearly low after Centene's stronger-than-expected medical loss ratio followed similar upbeat signals from UnitedHealth and Elevance, prompting analyst upgrades ahead of Q2 earnings.

headline: NHS delayed hospital discharges now cost £2.7 billion a year, King's Fund finds
summary: Analysis from the King's Fund shows the cost of patients stuck in hospital beds despite being medically fit for discharge rose 7.5% in a year, driven by strained social care and community services capacity.

headline: NICE greenlights two non-invasive tests to cut years-long endometriosis diagnosis delays
summary: NICE recommended NHS use of Endotest, a saliva-based biomarker test, and EndoSure, a gut-signal sensor test, for a three-year evidence-gathering period aimed at speeding endometriosis diagnosis in primary care.

headline: US annuity sales notch another record first half, RILA leads growth
summary: Finalized LIMRA data show second-quarter 2026 US annuity sales around $121 billion (revised down slightly from an initial $123.9B estimate), extending an 11-quarter streak above $100 billion and pushing first-half 2026 sales to a record $231.3 billion, with registered index-linked annuities (RILAs) growing fastest.

headline: Legacy Marketing and Malibu Life USA team up on new indexed annuity line
summary: Legacy Marketing Group struck a distribution partnership with Malibu Life USA to bring two new fixed indexed annuity products, PillarMark and SpireMark, to market through independent agents starting this month, issued by Malibu's Texas-domiciled carrier TruSpire.

headline: Indian insurer stocks jump on expected crackdown on distributor commissions
summary: Shares of HDFC Life, ICICI Prudential Life, SBI Life and Max Financial rallied as much as 5% after reports that India's insurance regulator IRDAI is preparing a consultation paper to cap or reduce commissions paid to banks and other distributors, a move investors expect to lower acquisition costs and lift margins.

headline: State AI-governance rules for insurers reach a tipping point in 2026
summary: Adoption of the NAIC's AI Model Bulletin has spread to roughly 25 US states as of mid-2026, with several more in progress, pushing carriers to build documented AI governance, testing and monitoring programs for underwriting and claims models as a new multistate examiner tool pilots across a dozen states.

headline: Luxembourg insurer OneLife completes CEO handover
summary: Cross-border life insurer OneLife confirmed Cédric Lootvoet as its new Chief Executive Officer effective September 1, 2026, succeeding Bruno Valersteinas after Lootvoet had spent roughly nine months as Deputy CEO preparing for the transition.

headline: Sun Life and Wilton Re launch new reinsurer to hunt bigger life and annuity blocks
summary: Sun Life and Wilton Re unveiled Windsor Life Re, a roughly $900 million jointly capitalized reinsurance vehicle domiciled in the US and Bermuda aimed at acquiring larger in-force life and annuity blocks, with Sun Life's SLC Management running the investment portfolio and an initial $1.7 billion book already being reinsured from Wilton Re.

headline: Full plan terminations now drive most pension risk transfer deals
summary: October Three's 2026 PRT Trends survey found plan terminations accounted for two-thirds of pension risk transfer transactions in the first half of 2026, with buy-in premiums up sharply even as total buyout dollar volume cooled from a strong 2025 finish, and carriers reporting less worry about PRT litigation than a year ago.

headline: DOL floats safe harbor for putting alternative assets into 401(k) menus
summary: The Department of Labor's proposed rule, issued March 31, 2026 under a 2025 White House executive order, would give plan fiduciaries a six-factor "prudent process" safe harbor for adding private equity, real estate and other alternative investments as 401(k) and 403(b) designated investment options.

headline: India's pension regulator overhauls NPS fees and lets banks sponsor pension funds
summary: PFRDA cleared scheduled banks to sponsor and run National Pension System pension funds under a new slab-based investment-management fee structure from April 2026, and separately clarified a revised CRA charge structure for NPS accounts taking effect July 1, 2026.

headline: Aging Asia-Pacific populations push pension providers toward income-focused products
summary: Amundi's research team flagged that rapidly aging populations in Japan, China, Australia and South Korea are shifting demand from pure accumulation toward decumulation and retirement-income products, as state and workplace pension systems in the region struggle to keep pace.

headline: 401(k) recordkeeper consolidation wave builds pressure on mid-tier providers
summary: Industry coverage points to an accelerating round of recordkeeper mergers and exits as scale, proprietary products and wealth-management capability increasingly separate winners from mid-tier record keepers squeezed by falling fees and rising technology costs.

headline: CVC finishes rollup of credit manager Marathon into new CVC-Marathon platform
summary: CVC Capital Partners completed its roughly $1.6 billion acquisition of Marathon Asset Management, rebranding the combined credit business as CVC-Marathon and pushing CVC Credit's fee-paying AUM to around €61 billion.

headline: Insurers lean into private credit and asset-backed bonds as spreads tighten
summary: Invesco's mid-year 2026 insurance investment outlook shows carriers making incremental rather than sweeping portfolio shifts, favoring investment-grade, asset-backed and structurally protected private credit as spreads compress to mid-5% yields in the US/UK and mid-3% in Europe.

headline: Grayscale pushes crypto further into mainstream advisor portfolios
summary: Grayscale rolled out digital-asset model portfolios for financial advisors in mid-September 2026, giving wealth managers a packaged way to add crypto exposure to client accounts as digital assets keep edging into traditional asset-management platforms.

headline: BNP Paribas Asset Management installs four new co-CIOs
summary: BNP Paribas Asset Management named four new Chief Investment Officers, including Guy Davies as Deputy Global Head of Investments and CIO for fundamental active equity and Robinson Rouchié as CIO for systematic and quantitative investments, effective September 1, 2026, reporting to global investments head Rob Gambi as part of the firm's "AMplify 2030" plan.

headline: AGF's August AUM snapshot shows steady asset growth
summary: Canadian asset manager AGF reported total assets under management and fee-earning assets of roughly $74.2 billion as of August 31, 2026, offering an early read on how markets and flows treated mid-tier managers heading into the fall.

headline: Wealth-manager tie-ups keep asset and wealth management dealmaking hot
summary: PwC's mid-2026 US deals outlook found asset and wealth management M&A holding up despite macro uncertainty, with first-quarter 2026 deal volume hitting 109 transactions - the highest quarterly total in two years - and wealth-management consolidation driving roughly three-quarters of that activity.

headline: RIA consolidation wave keeps building as serial acquirers hit new AUM milestones
summary: Nationwide RIA deal volume has climbed roughly 40% year-over-year through mid-2026, with active platform buyers like Beacon Pointe, Savant and Mercer Advisors racking up multiple tuck-in acquisitions this year while a smaller number of platform-scale deals account for an outsized share of assets changing hands.

headline: Fintech investors keep favoring wealthtech in a blockbuster funding week
summary: More than $1.3 billion was raised across a dozen fintech deals in a single week in early September, extending a 2026 pattern where investors are writing fewer but much larger checks into wealth management, financial infrastructure and enterprise automation startups.

headline: New AI platform aims to cut adviser admin time for independent wealth firms
summary: WealthAi went live with an AI platform built for independent financial advisers, with beta testing reportedly cutting routine client-administration time by roughly 60%, part of a broader 2026 push to embed AI into front-office advisory workflows rather than just back-office tasks.

headline: India's wealth management market on track to more than double by the mid-2030s
summary: India's wealth-management industry is projected to roughly 2.5x to about $436 billion by 2034, fueled by a 90% four-year jump in dollar-millionaire households and mutual fund AUM approaching Rs 78 lakh crore, according to industry estimates cited in early September coverage.

headline: SEC pushes forward on adviser recordkeeping and fiduciary-conduct rulemaking
summary: The SEC published a proposed rule amendment in the Federal Register on September 10 updating books-and-records requirements for investment advisers, part of a broader FY2026 exam agenda emphasizing fiduciary standards, conflict-of-interest disclosure and Regulation S-P cybersecurity compliance.

headline: Chicago RIA Choreo taps another Edelman veteran for newly created executive post
summary: Choreo named Kelly O'Donnell as its first chief people and transformation officer, marking the fourth Edelman Financial Engines alum hired into a C-suite role at the RIA in about a year; she will oversee HR, brand and the integration of acquired firms.

headline: Mapfre's buyout of Safety Insurance clears key antitrust hurdle
summary: The regulatory waiting period on Mapfre's acquisition of Safety Insurance Group expired on September 14, clearing the way for Safety to become a wholly owned Mapfre subsidiary after shareholder materials were mailed the same week.

headline: US P&C insurers post stronger profits even as premium growth cools sharply
summary: Industry-wide net underwriting gains more than doubled to $31.7 billion in the first half of 2026, even as net written premium growth slowed to about 2.1% from 5.2% a year earlier, with personal auto and commercial property rates softening while liability and casualty losses kept worsening.

headline: India overhauls insurer capital and ownership rules under new reform package
summary: IRDAI approved amended regulations covering insurer registration, capital structure and amalgamation, part of a broader 2026 reform push under the new insurance-law amendment act that also enabled two insurers to raise foreign ownership above the old 74% cap following the move to permit 100% FDI.

headline: AIG's general insurance chief to step down at year-end
summary: AIG confirmed that its general insurance CEO, Lou Hancock, will retire at the end of 2026, adding to a string of senior leadership moves at the carrier this quarter as it resets its executive bench.

headline: Claims handling starts shifting from AI-assisted to AI-run workflows
summary: Industry commentary this month points to 2026-2027 as the inflection point where US P&C claims move from adjusters simply using AI tools to more autonomous, agentic systems that orchestrate a claim end-to-end while a human reviews the outcome.

headline: Aon strikes $17 billion deal for rival broker USI to bulk up in the middle market
summary: Aon agreed to buy USI Insurance Services from KKR for $17 billion in cash, following its earlier NFP purchase, aiming to build a leading middle-market platform and expand access to the excess-and-surplus lines market; USI's CEO will become Aon's global middle-market chief once the deal closes in Q4 2026.

headline: UK consolidator Clear Group buys specialist Lloyd's wholesale broker
summary: Clear Group acquired Newman Pearce & Partners, a 24-person Lloyd's wholesale broker whose revenue grew from about £5m to £7m in the past year, as part of Clear's push to deepen its London market wholesale broking presence.

headline: Cyber-focused MGA Trivora lands growth capital from private equity backer
summary: Trivora Insurance, a specialty cyber MGA for small and mid-sized businesses, secured a growth investment led by Carroll Street Capital, which also gets a board seat and a right of first refusal on future acquisition financing as Trivora expands into new specialty lines.

headline: Specialty insurer Mosaic rolls out AI-driven underwriting platform for SMEs
summary: Mosaic Insurance launched a digital underwriting system called HALO that combines broker trading activity, underwriting decisions and portfolio outcomes in one environment, aimed at speeding up delivery of complex specialty products to small and midsize business customers.

headline: Asia-Pacific insurance dealmaking cools even as India and Malaysia buck the trend
summary: Broader M&A activity across Asia-Pacific's insurance and broking sector slowed in the second quarter of 2026, even as India and Malaysia each recorded major multi-million-dollar transactions, underscoring uneven momentum across the region's markets.

headline: Marsh names new global chief claims officer as it reshuffles claims leadership
summary: Marsh Risk appointed Chetna Gulati-Kapoor, a 20-year claims veteran who trained as a solicitor in India and the UK, as global chief claims officer effective September 1, succeeding Rob Powell, who moves up to chairman of global claims.

headline: AI-native claims TPA Elysian bolsters leadership with new claims strategy chief
summary: Elysian, a startup positioning itself as an AI-native third-party administrator for complex commercial claims, named industry veteran Armando Andrade as its Head of Claims Strategy, bringing over two decades of TPA and claims-operations experience from TheBest Claims Solutions.

headline: Fiduciary Services Group buys Vermont retirement-plan TPA Future Planning Associates
summary: Retirement-plan administration consolidator Fiduciary Services Group acquired Future Planning Associates, a Vermont-based third-party administrator and recordkeeping firm, marking FSG's third TPA acquisition in about 14 months as consolidation continues in benefits administration.

headline: IRDAI finalizes feedback on proposed overhaul of TPA health-services rules
summary: India's insurance regulator IRDAI published its formal response to stakeholder comments on draft amendments to the Third Party Administrators (Health Services) Regulations, agreeing to clarify certificate-renewal requirements and cancellation procedures for TPAs after a public consultation that closed in mid-2026.

headline: Zinnia adds whole-life product engine to its Zahara administration platform
summary: Life and annuity technology vendor Zinnia expanded its Zahara policy administration system with a new configurable whole-life chassis aimed at the final-expense market, letting carriers launch products in roughly three months as API-based, cloud-native administration continues replacing legacy batch systems.

headline: Wealthtech giant FNZ secures $450m top-up from existing backers
summary: Global wealth-management technology platform FNZ raised $450 million in new equity from long-standing institutional investors including CPP Investments and La Caisse, earmarking the funds for continued platform modernization, hiring and product expansion.

headline: Embedded-insurance infrastructure firm Cover Genius raises $100m to scale AI protection tools
summary: Cover Genius, which powers embedded insurance for e-commerce and travel platforms, closed a $100 million round lifting its valuation to roughly $1.9 billion, with proceeds going toward AI-driven personalization, automated claims handling and agentic distribution of coverage.

headline: New Indian insurer Protec taps insureMO to build an AI-native policy core
summary: Newly licensed general insurer Protec General Insurance selected middle-office platform provider insureMO to build an API-driven, AI-native insurance core system, aiming to speed its rollout of retail and commercial products across India.

headline: Captive-manager platform Luzern Risk closes $45m Series B
summary: Luzern Risk, a full-service captive insurance manager offering alternative risk-financing structures, raised a $45 million Series B round, part of a busy mid-September week in which fintech firms collectively raised over $850 million.

headline: Fintech venture funding climbs 23% in H1 2026 even as deal count drops sharply
summary: Crunchbase data shows global venture funding into fintech startups rose nearly 23% year-over-year to $28.6 billion in the first half of 2026, even as deal count fell more than 25%, reflecting investors concentrating larger checks into AI, wealth management and financial-infrastructure plays.

headline: Insurance software vendor Insurity elevates Jatin Atre to chief executive
summary: Insurance technology provider Insurity promoted Jatin Atre, who had served as president since January 2026, to chief executive officer, succeeding Jeff Clarke, as the company pushes to accelerate AI-powered products for brokers and carriers.

headline: UK broker JMG Group names Andrew Cunis to lead South and private-client business
summary: UK insurance broker consolidator JMG Group appointed industry veteran Andrew Cunis, who brings more than 22 years of experience, as chief executive of its South of England and private-client operations as the group continues regional expansion.

headline: Munich Re to buy cyber insurtech At-Bay for $575 million
summary: Munich Re's Hartford Steam Boiler unit is converting its long-running capacity partnership with At-Bay into outright ownership, picking up the MGA's cyber underwriting platform and security-monitoring data assets. The deal values At-Bay at roughly 2x its $278M gross written premium and is expected to close in Q1 2027.

headline: AI-native startups swallow nearly all insurtech venture funding in Q2
summary: Gallagher Re's latest tally shows global insurtech investment jumped to a four-year-high $2.44 billion across 95 deals in Q2 2026, with AI-focused underwriting, claims and fraud platforms absorbing about 99% of that capital.

headline: US commercial carriers scramble to absorb 2026 ISO liability overhaul
summary: A major rewrite of ISO's Commercial General Liability classification and pricing framework is forcing US property-casualty insurers to update rating, governance and filing processes mid-cycle, adding operational strain heading into year-end renewals.

headline: State regulators wrap pilot of new AI governance exam tool for insurers
summary: NAIC's multistate pilot of its AI Systems Evaluation Tool, which gives market-conduct examiners a standardized way to probe insurers' algorithmic governance, has been running since January and concludes this month, reinforcing that existing insurance law applies however underwriting or claims decisions are automated.

headline: AIG's top P&C executive Jon Hancock to step down at year-end
summary: AIG disclosed that General Insurance CEO Jon Hancock will retire December 31, 2026 and move into a senior advisory role reporting to CEO Eric Andersen, the latest in a string of leadership changes atop the carrier this year.

headline: French digital health insurer Alan raises €480M to push into Canada
summary: Alan closed a Prosus-led Series G of roughly $550M at a €5.5B valuation, with Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan returning for a third round; the Paris-based carrier says it topped €800M in annualized revenue in Q1 2026 and is using the capital to scale its newly licensed Canadian health plan business.

headline: Florida clears HCSC's absorption of Cigna's local Medicare business
summary: Florida's insurance commissioner signed off on Health Care Service Corp's acquisition of Cigna's HealthSpring Medicare Advantage operations in the state, one of the remaining state-level approvals needed to fully fold Cigna's Medicare book into HCSC.

headline: Cigna hands the CEO job to Brian Evanko as Cordani steps back
summary: The Cigna Group announced that President and COO Brian Evanko will succeed David Cordani as chief executive effective July 1, 2026, with Cordani shifting to executive chair — one of several long-tenured payer CEOs to exit this year.

headline: ACA enrollees hit with the subsidy cliff again as enhanced credits lapse
summary: With the pandemic-era enhanced premium tax credits gone as of January 1, 2026, the ACA's hard income cutoff for subsidy eligibility has returned, and marketplace insurers' median proposed rate increase for 2026 sits around 18-20%, pushing many middle-income households toward much higher net premiums.

headline: Congress locks in long-debated PBM transparency reforms
summary: The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 folds in significant pharmacy benefit manager reform aimed at delinking PBM compensation from drug prices and improving fee disclosure, arriving alongside a separate FTC settlement that forces changes to Express Scripts' PBM practices.

headline: Big payers say AI-driven prior-auth cleanup is cutting transaction volume
summary: The six largest publicly traded insurers report they've standardized documentation for more than half their prior-authorization requests under an industry pledge, and sector-wide prior-auth volume has fallen about 11% over a 10-month stretch as automated, standardized workflows take hold.

headline: Employer medical plan cost inflation eases slightly across Asia-Pacific
summary: Brokers report that year-over-year medical trend increases for corporate health plans across Asia-Pacific markets are moderating somewhat in 2026 compared with recent years, though costs remain elevated as insurers cite an aging population and rising private-care demand.

headline: Sanford Health completes tie-up with North Memorial Health in the Twin Cities
summary: Sanford Health finalized its partnership with North Memorial Health on September 1, 2026, giving Sanford an anchor presence in the Minneapolis-St. Paul market as part of a broader wave of hospital consolidation moving through 2026.

headline: Clinical AI keeps pulling outsized venture dollars in digital health's rebound
summary: US digital health startups raised $7.4B in the first half of 2026, up from $6.4B a year earlier, with clinical-workflow AI a standout category; radiology-AI platform Aidoc alone landed its second $150M check in under a year.

headline: Hospital margins keep sliding as expenses outrun reimbursement
summary: System-wide operating margins fell roughly 5% nationally in early 2026 versus a year earlier, with rising bad debt and uncompensated care, soft government reimbursement and Medicare Advantage payment friction squeezing smaller hospitals hardest while the largest nonprofit systems hold up better.

headline: Taiwan's hospitals roll out agentic AI at scale with NVIDIA and Foxconn
summary: Under a $1.5B 'Healthy Taiwan' push, Foxconn and the island's leading medical centers are deploying NVIDIA-powered clinical agents for tasks like ECG screening, cancer subtyping and real-time procedural support, covering over 14 million patient encounters a year.

headline: Ambient-AI vendor Suki pushes past documentation into standalone dictation tools
summary: Clinical scribe company Suki is broadening its ambient AI suite with a modular, standalone dictation product for EHRs, part of a wider push by ambient-documentation vendors to extend beyond note-taking into fuller clinical workflow support.

headline: CMS locks in more than 5,500 specialists for its mandatory 2027 payment model
summary: CMS released the final participant roster for its new Ambulatory Specialty Model, compelling 5,556 specialists treating heart failure and low back pain in selected regions into value-based payment starting January 1, 2027, with the program running five performance years.

headline: ChristianaCare taps Jenn Schwartz as next CEO
summary: Delaware-based ChristianaCare named Jenn Schwartz as its incoming chief executive, succeeding longtime CEO Janice Nevin, who retired September 1, 2026, as part of a broader wave of health-system leadership turnover this year.
